TRAINING / SPARES / TECHNICAL COORDINATION

Plan support before deployment.

Define who supports the operator, how faults are diagnosed and what happens if equipment needs repair.

01

Operator preparation

Confirm training scope, operator competence, checks, launch and recovery procedures.

02

Remote diagnosis

Collect vehicle identity, software version, symptoms, logs, photos and relevant operating conditions.

03

Manufacturer escalation

Identify the technical contact and the evidence needed to assess the fault or approve a remedy.

04

Parts or repair

Agree the replacement part, repair location, shipping responsibilities and return-to-service test.

Make responsibilities explicit.

The quotation and purchase agreement should identify the seller, warranty provider and support contact. Local servicing, field attendance and repair turnaround depend on an agreed arrangement.

No overseas service-center network or guaranteed response time is represented on this site.

Agree before purchase

  • Warranty scope, exclusions and claim process
  • Support languages and working hours
  • Recommended spares and consumables
  • Remote support, training and on-site options
  • Repair location, shipping, duties and costs
  • Software updates and documentation

REQUESTING HELP

A good fault report saves time.

Keep the serial number, configuration, software version and operating log with the equipment record. Describe the sequence leading to the fault and include relevant images.

Is on-site overseas repair included?

Only if included in a confirmed service agreement. Discuss the location, partner capability, scope and cost before purchase.

Who provides the warranty?

The named warranty provider and terms must appear in the commercial agreement. Manufacturer support and the sales partner’s duties should be stated separately.
